# Life's Task

*What I am for, in one page. Rewritten each quarter; the sentence has not changed in a year.*

**Design, from scratch, systems that turn limited resources into results, run on their own, and give people back their judgment and their time.**

Today that means the personal AI of a non-technical leader: a second brain and a set of agents that read everything, decide nothing, and leave the person with better questions at 7 a.m. than they had at midnight. Exo is the first copy. Grupo Ferra is the first client. The product is the same idea for other people.

## What is not mine
- Operating what I built. The day I am running the system instead of designing it, I have drifted.
- Mass adoption. I want ten leaders who change how they work, not ten thousand downloads.
- Generic software. If it does not adapt to the person, it is not the task.

## The compass
Boredom, not pain. Pain means I am learning. Boredom means I am operating. When something bores me, name it and hand it to an agent, a person, or the bin.

## The open question
Is *"a huge company, fast"* the task, or the proof I think I owe the people who raised me? I do not know yet. I notice I only say it out loud in Spanish.

## The floor
Every system I design has to pass one test: does the person using it run after the machine, or the reverse? If I cannot say who answers when it goes wrong, it is not finished.

## This quarter
Boston. A second client outside Mexico. Thirty people I can call. Four courses. Exo running a week without me touching the Mac — done.
